entries.subject: The symmetric and antisymmetric ZDI reconstructions
entries.finding: The deposit holds three reconstructions per epoch; the paper's Figs. 1-3 show the unconstrained one, which is shown here. The constrained sets test how robust the maps are.
entries.revisitWhen: A reader asks to compare reconstructions.

entries.subject: The meridional field component
entries.finding: Each map also carries B_M; the paper's cycle analysis (butterfly diagrams) uses the radial and azimuthal components, which are shown here.
entries.revisitWhen: The meridional component is needed to explain something shown.

entries.subject: The giant planet iota Horologii b
entries.finding: The star hosts a giant planet at about 1 au (Alvarado-Gomez et al. 2023, citing the radial-velocity discovery). No three-dimensional orbit of it is used in this package yet, so it is not placed.
entries.revisitWhen: A published three-dimensional orbit of the planet is added.

entries.subject: The direction of the spin axis on the sky
entries.finding: ZDI gives the axis's tilt to the line of sight (60 degrees adopted) but not its position angle, which is set toward celestial north.
entries.revisitWhen: Interferometry or another method measures the axis's position angle.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 6,080 K and log g 4.4 (u1 0.402, u2 0.292): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. Gravity: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/iota-horologii.json: 4.399.
